quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #23
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: School zone speed limits are always 25 mph.
questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: School zones in Nevada have speed limits of either 15 mph or 25 mph. These limits apply on school days from 30 minutes before school starts to 30 minutes after school ends, unless a different speed is posted.

questions.question: When parking uphill next to a curb, set the parking brake and:

options.text: Keep the rear tires against the curb.
Keep the front tires straight ahead.
Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
Turn your steering wheel toward the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill next to a curb, set the parking brake and turn your steering wheel away from the curb. If your car rolls, it will roll toward the curb and stop.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: You must bear either right or left.
A road joins from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must bear either right or left.
questions.explanation: This sign shows a Y intersection ahead. You must choose to go right or left.

questions.question: What does a single dashed white line between lanes mean?

options.text: Drivers may pass, even if it could be dangerous.
Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. Dashed white lines can be crossed to pass or change lanes if it is safe.

questions.question: When using a roundabout, drivers should:

options.text: Yield to traffic already in the roundabout.
Stop in the middle of the roundabout.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to traffic already in the roundabout.
questions.explanation: A roundabout is a circular intersection with traffic flowing counterclockwise around a center island. When entering, yield to cars already in the roundabout. Follow the circle until you reach your exit.

questions.question: When driving on slippery roads:

options.text: Always drive at the maximum speed limit.
Use cruise control to maintain a steady speed.
Do not make any sudden changes in speed or direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not make any sudden changes in speed or direction.
questions.explanation: Avoid sudden changes in speed or direction on slippery surfaces. Reduce your speed and do not use cruise control.

questions.question: What does a single dashed yellow line between lanes mean?

options.text: Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.
Both lanes travel in the same direction.
Drivers may pass, even if it could be dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A single dashed yellow line means both directions can pass. You may only pass if it is safe and you won't interfere with oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When the traffic light turns yellow as you approach an intersection, you should:

options.text: Consider it a caution sign and continue through the intersection.
Stop before entering the intersection, unless you are too close to stop safely.
Speed up to get through before the red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection, unless you are too close to stop safely.
questions.explanation: When you see a yellow light, slow down and stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are too close to stop, drive carefully through.

questions.question: If you need to stop quickly and your vehicle does not have Anti-Lock Brakes (ABS), you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Firmly pump your brakes.
questions.explanation: Pumping the brakes is the best way to stop quickly without ABS. This stops the car fast and lets you keep steering control.

questions.question: This sign shows one type of:
questions.correctAnswerText: Intersection.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that an intersection with a crossing road is ahead.

questions.question: You hear a siren while driving but cannot see the emergency vehicle yet. What should you do?

options.text: Keep driving until you see the vehicle.
Pull to the curb and look to see if the vehicle is on your street.
Slow down but don't stop until you see it.
Speed up and turn at the next intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the curb and look to see if the vehicle is on your street.
questions.explanation: If you hear a siren but do not know where the emergency vehicle is, safely pull over to the right side of the road and stop. Wait until you are sure the vehicle is not coming toward you.

questions.question: What does a "No standing" sign mean?

options.text: You may never stop your vehicle there.
You may park there if the driver stays in the vehicle.
You may stop briefly to pick up or drop off passengers.
You may stop to load or unload goods.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may stop briefly to pick up or drop off passengers.
questions.explanation: A "No standing" sign means you may only make a brief stop to pick up or drop off passengers.

questions.question: You are in an accident and your vehicle is blocking traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Move your vehicle off the road if you can.
Do not move your vehicle under any circumstances.
Wait for police to arrive before moving your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your vehicle off the road if you can.
questions.explanation: After a minor accident, move your vehicle off the road if possible. Do not leave the scene without identifying yourself and helping those who need it.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow arrow traffic signal mean?

options.text: It is not used as a traffic signal.
It means the same thing as a yellow traffic light.
Drivers may turn in the direction of the arrow.
A green arrow is about to appear.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means the same thing as a yellow traffic light.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow arrow means the same as a yellow traffic light. When you see it, slow down and be ready to stop at a red light.

questions.question: What best keeps you and others safe when backing up your vehicle?

options.text: Honk your horn right before shifting into reverse.
Check behind the vehicle before you get in the driver's seat.
Turn up the car radio to alert people around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind the vehicle before you get in the driver's seat.
questions.explanation: Backing is risky because drivers cannot see well behind their vehicles. Before getting in to back up, walk to the back of the vehicle and check for children and small objects.

questions.question: How can you check your blind spots when changing lanes?

options.text: Use both inside and outside rearview mirrors.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Turn your head to check your blind spots before every lane change.

questions.question: When driving in bad weather, what should you do?

options.text: Drive faster to reach your destination sooner.
Follow the car ahead more closely.
Stay farther back from the car ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther back from the car ahead.
questions.explanation: When driving on wet roads, increase the distance between your vehicle and the one ahead.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a traffic signal is coming. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: When driving to an unfamiliar area, what should you do?

options.text: Rely on road signs to find your way.
Plan your trip before you leave.
You only need a general idea of where you are going.
Always take the most direct route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan your trip before you leave.
questions.explanation: Plan your trip before driving to an unfamiliar area. Check a map to find your destination before you start driving. Do not start with just a vague idea of where you are going.

questions.question: What helps prevent crashes?

options.text: Drive only on side streets and back roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Communicate with other road users.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do something others do not expect. Communicate with other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians by signaling when you slow down, stop, or turn. Use your lights and horn when needed.

questions.question: When a car is coming toward you with bright headlights, what should you do?

options.text: Use your bright lights until the other car dims theirs.
Flash your lights on and off to warn the other driver.
Dim your lights and then speed up to pass quickly.
Look toward the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: If a car is coming toward you with high beams on, look away from the headlights. Look toward the right side of the road until the car passes. This keeps you from being blinded.

questions.question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?
questions.correctAnswerText: Human error
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do not see other vehicles or when a driver does something unexpected. Talk to other drivers on the road to help prevent crashes.

questions.question: When you are entering a roundabout, you should always:
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, slow down. Roundabouts are designed to be driven at low speed.

questions.question: When you see a steady green arrow on a traffic signal, you:

options.text: Should move into a lane in the direction of the arrow.
Should slow down and stop if it is safe.
May turn in the direction of the arrow after letting traffic and pedestrians in the intersection go first.
May drive straight through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: May turn in the direction of the arrow after letting traffic and pedestrians in the intersection go first.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you may turn in the direction of the arrow. You must be in the correct lane for this turn. Let any vehicles and pedestrians already in the intersection go first.

questions.question: On a two-lane road with a single solid yellow line on your side, can you pass other cars?
questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: When there is a solid and broken yellow line between lanes going opposite directions, you may only pass when the broken yellow line is on your side.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Turn right after making a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot turn right.
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign that shows traffic rules you must follow. This sign means right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What is used on some highways to show drivers which lanes to use for turning?

options.text: White lines on the side of the road
White arrows in the middle of the lanes

questions.correctAnswerText: White arrows in the middle of the lanes
questions.explanation: White arrows in the lanes show which lanes to use for driving straight or turning.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Deer may cross here.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that deer cross the road in this area. Slow down, pay attention, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign that shows rules drivers must follow. It means right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What is the leading cause of traffic accidents in Nevada?

options.text: Not giving the right-of-way when required.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not giving the right-of-way when required.
questions.explanation: Not giving the right-of-way is the leading cause of traffic accidents in Nevada. Learn Nevada's right-of-way rules and always be ready to give up your right-of-way to prevent accidents.

questions.question: You should drive below the speed limit when:

options.text: Road or weather conditions are not perfect.
You are entering a highway with other cars.
You are on a four-lane road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road or weather conditions are not perfect.
questions.explanation: Drive below the speed limit when roads are wet, visibility is poor, or any condition is unsafe. Even if you are within the speed limit, you can be ticketed for driving too fast for the conditions.

questions.question: You cannot park within ____ of a railroad crossing.
questions.correctAnswerText: 50 feet
questions.explanation: Never park within 50 feet of a railroad crossing. Park only in legal spots where drivers from both directions can clearly see your vehicle.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, you should:

options.text: Keep the front wheels straight and set the parking brake.
Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
Turn the front wheels toward the curb.
Turn the back wheels into the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels sharply away from the curb when parking uphill. If your brakes fail, your car will roll into the curb instead of into traffic.

questions.question: A curb painted ____ means a loading zone or parking restriction.
questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: Painted curbs show parking rules. Yellow curbs mark loading zones or other parking restrictions.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Lane ends.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow and black. They alert drivers to hazards ahead. This sign tells you a lane is ending and you need to prepare for traffic to merge safely.

questions.question: When exiting a highway, you should slow down:

options.text: On the main road, just before the exit lane.
Once you see a toll booth.
After you have moved into the exit lane.
When you first see the exit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: After you have moved into the exit lane.
questions.explanation: Move into the exit lane well in advance. Wait until you are in the exit lane before you start slowing down.

questions.question: When you see a steady yellow arrow light, you should:

options.text: Merge in the direction of the arrow.
Slow down and stop, if it is safe to do so.
Turn left after checking for oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Have the right-of-way and expect oncoming traffic to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop, if it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow arrow means a red arrow is coming next. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: Crosswalks are:

options.text: Either marked with lines or not marked at all.

questions.correctAnswerText: Either marked with lines or not marked at all.
questions.explanation: Crosswalks exist whether they are marked or not. Stop behind any crosswalk to let pedestrians go first.

questions.question: When a green light appears, you should:

options.text: Speed up as fast as possible.
Wait for another driver to wave you on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let pedestrians cross first.
questions.explanation: A green light means you can go. However, first yield to pedestrians and traffic still in the intersection.

questions.question: An oncoming driver does not dim their high beams. Where should you look?

options.text: At the wheels of the other vehicle.
Toward the right side of the road.
Toward the left side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded and lets you see enough road to stay on course until the other vehicle passes.

questions.question: When driving through an area where children are playing, what should you expect?

options.text: They know when it is safe to cross the street.
They will stop at the curb before crossing.
They may run in front of you without looking.
They will not cross unless an adult is with them.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may run in front of you without looking.
questions.explanation: Always slow down and be extra careful when children are nearby. Children may not understand danger and could run in front of your vehicle without looking.

questions.question: Which traffic light means you must stop, let others pass, then go when it is safe?
questions.correctAnswerText: A flashing red light.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop completely, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: Roads freeze quickly in which areas?
questions.correctAnswerText: Shaded areas.
questions.explanation: In cold or wet weather, be careful on roads shaded by trees or buildings. These areas freeze faster than other parts of the road and take longer to dry.

questions.question: A sign says "Reduced speed, 35 mph." What does this mean?

options.text: The new speed limit of 35 mph starts at this sign.
The new speed limit of 35 mph starts at the next sign.
You have plenty of time to slow down before the zone starts.
You should only go 35 mph in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: The new speed limit of 35 mph starts at this sign.
questions.explanation: "Reduced speed" signs tell drivers to slow down. The new speed limit begins at the sign.

questions.question: You turn onto a two-lane road with a broken yellow line. What does this tell you?

options.text: Traffic flows in both directions on this road.
Traffic flows in only one direction on this road.
You must stay to the left of the yellow lines.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic flows in both directions on this road.
questions.explanation: Yellow center lines separate traffic going in opposite directions. A broken yellow line means you can pass slower traffic when it is safe.

questions.question: What happens if a bicyclist breaks traffic laws?

options.text: Bicyclists do not have to follow traffic laws.
They will always get a warning from police.
Their bicycle will be taken away.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can be ticketed.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists have the same rights and responsibilities as drivers. Both can be ticketed for breaking traffic laws.

questions.question: When passing a vehicle on a two-lane road, when should you return to your lane?

options.text: When you have enough space between you and the vehicle you passed.
Stay in the left lane if you plan to turn left.
You can drive in either lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you have enough space between you and the vehicle you passed.
questions.explanation: When passing on a two-lane road, return to the right lane when there is enough space between you and the vehicle you passed.

questions.question: On a freeway, how far ahead should you look?
questions.correctAnswerText: 20 to 30 seconds ahead
questions.explanation: Look 20 to 30 seconds ahead on the freeway. This helps you avoid sudden stops or unexpected turns.

questions.question: How far from a crosswalk must you park?
questions.correctAnswerText: At least 20 feet
questions.explanation: Do not park within 20 feet of a crosswalk. Park only where it is legal and where other drivers can see your vehicle clearly.

questions.question: What do round signs warn about?
questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossings ahead.
questions.explanation: Round signs warn drivers about railroad crossings. Be extra careful when you see these signs.
